plan_a_advantages: Plan A includes cross-training, which can provide a broader base of fitness and reduce the risk of overuse injuries.

plan_b_advantages: Plan B is more specific to the goal of becoming a faster trail runner by focusing solely on trail running.
The longer run durations in Plan B (especially the 90-minute run) provide a greater stimulus for aerobic development and endurance on trails.
The consistent trail running in Plan B allows for better adaptation to trail-specific challenges and skill development.
Plan B provides more total training volume (269 minutes vs 227 minutes) which can contribute to greater fitness gains.
reasoning: Given the goal of becoming a faster trail runner, Plan B appears to be the better choice.
